faw_title: Check maize for Fall Armyworm early
faw_hint: Check young maize before damage spreads
faw_tagline: Early maize checks for Ga-Matlapa and Mankweng
faw_intro: Inspect several plants across your field, including the underside of leaves and the central rolled leaves (whorl). Answer for what you actually see.
faw_sample: Sample decision support, not a confirmed diagnosis. Local agronomic validation and Sepedi speaker review are pending.
faw_offline: This checklist and guidance are bundled for offline use after the first online load. No account is needed.
faw_required: Answer each question, using Not sure when you cannot tell.
faw_windows: Are there tiny holes or pale, thin patches like windows on young leaves?
faw_eggs: Are there clusters of eggs or small caterpillars on the leaves?
faw_damage: Are there ragged holes or sawdust-like droppings in the central rolled leaves?
faw_possible: Possible FAW signs — inspect and seek confirmation
faw_unknown: Uncertain — inspect again with an adviser
faw_possible_desc: These signs can have other causes. This checklist cannot confirm FAW or measure outbreak severity.
faw_unknown_desc: Uncertain answers cannot rule out FAW. Ask a local agricultural extension adviser to inspect affected maize.
faw_clear_desc: No reported signs does not rule out hidden eggs or larvae. Keep scouting young maize.
faw_scout: Walk through different parts of the field. Look closely at young leaves, underneath leaves and inside the whorl for eggs and caterpillars.
faw_remove: If you identify FAW egg clusters or young caterpillars, remove and crush them by hand where reachable. Preserve beneficial insects.
faw_record: Record the date, affected plants and where you found signs in your farm logbook. Check nearby maize as well.
faw_adviser: Ask your local agricultural extension adviser serving Ga-Matlapa or Mankweng to confirm the pest, especially if damage spreads or larvae are hard to reach.
faw_chemical: Before using any pesticide, get local advice and follow the registered product label. Do not guess a dose or measure it with bottle caps.
faw_monitor: Revisit the field regularly during early maize growth and check for fresh damage, eggs and young caterpillars.
faw_reference: Offline reference: early feeding may leave pinholes or thin window-like patches; larger larvae can cause ragged damage and droppings. Similar damage can come from other pests.
faw_draft: FAW guidance is shown in English for this language. Sepedi is available in the language menu.
